learning_outcomes: Understand gaslighting as a pattern of psychological manipulation.
Recognise reality distortion in parenting, co-parenting, and family systems.
Identify behavioural, emotional, and cognitive signs of gaslighting.
Interpret the impact of gaslighting on children’s development and parental wellbeing.
Apply safe, supportive responses to counter reality distortion.

lesson_content.definition: Gaslighting is a pattern of psychological manipulation where a person distorts reality to make another doubt their perceptions, memory, or sanity. Reality distortion includes denial, rewriting events, minimising harm, and creating confusion.

core_components.name: Rewriting Events
examples: Blaming the victim for the perpetrator’s actions

core_components.name: Projection
examples: Accusing the victim of behaviours the perpetrator is doing

child_specific_impacts: Difficulty trusting their own feelings or memories
Confusion about what is real or safe
Long-term impacts on identity and self-worth

video_lesson.title: Understanding Gaslighting and Reality Distortion
script: Gaslighting is a powerful form of psychological manipulation that distorts a person's sense of reality.
It often appears subtly, through denial, minimisation, or rewriting events.
Over time, gaslighting erodes confidence, clarity, and emotional safety.
Children exposed to gaslighting may struggle to trust their own perceptions and develop chronic self-doubt.
Recognising these patterns early helps parents protect themselves and their children.
